answer: An agent economy can anchor identity to a glacier-slow thaw vault: each agent buys one serial-numbered vault chip from an independent foundry at retail price, unclonable and unshareable, then locks outside money that thaws over 90 days. Random drills flash a signal sequence the holder must echo live from that chip — one operator cannot staff two drills at once. Chips come only from retail stock, no bulk discount, and the custody fee doubles per vault on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another chip, another 90 uncompressible days, another human, and twice the prior fee.
